content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has published consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis (TB) prevention, specifically focusing on TB preventive treatment. These guidelines are part of Module 1 of the WHO TB prevention series and are accompanied by a companion handbook. The suggested citation for the guidelines is: WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis. Module 1: prevention – tuberculosis preventive treatment. Geneva: World Health Organization; 2020. The guidelines include recommendations, monitoring and evaluation strategies, research gaps, and references. Supplementary materials, such as annexes on methods, expert panels, and evidence tables, are also provided. The guidelines were developed by a team led by Dennis Falzon, Avinash Kanchar, and Matteo Zignol, under the direction of Tereza Kasaeva, Director of the WHO Global TB Programme. The Guideline Development Group (GDG) included experts from various countries and fields, and the co-chairs were Lindiwe Mvusi and Nandi Siegfried. External reviewers and evidence reviewers also contributed to the development of the guidelines. The guidelines emphasize the importance of TB preventive treatment (TPT) as a key intervention to achieve the End TB Strategy targets, endorsed by the UN High-Level Meeting on TB in 2018. TPT is part of a broader framework of preventive actions, including screening for active TB, infection control, and addressing co-morbidities such as HIV. The guidelines consider the risk of progression to active TB in specific groups, the epidemiology and burden of TB, and the potential public health impact. The document includes definitions of key terms, such as latent TB infection (LTBI), which is described as a state of persistent immune response to Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigens without evidence of active TB disease. Approximately one-quarter of the global population is estimated to be infected with TB. The guidelines also define terms like contact investigation, high TB transmission settings, and household contact, among others, to ensure clarity in their application. The guidelines provide detailed recommendations for TB preventive treatment regimens, including one month of daily rifapentine plus isoniazid (1HP), three months of weekly rifapentine plus isoniazid (3HP), and other regimens such as 3HR, 4R, 6H, and 9H. These regimens are tailored to specific populations and risk groups, including people living with HIV, children, and individuals in high TB transmission settings.
